findings.passage: “Secure elections are fundamental to a functioning democracy,” State Rep. Dave Armstrong (R-Rice Lake) said.
findings.note: Quote in his office's release on the Assembly's approval of the photo ID constitutional amendment.

findings.passage: A commonsense photo ID requirement for voters has been part of the Wisconsin Statutes for years, but given the importance of election integrity, it makes sense to protect this safeguard by putting it into the state constitution.
findings.note: Same release. He supports putting the photo ID requirement in the state constitution.

findings.passage: I supported this proposal last session, when it came up for the first time, and I voted for it again today.
findings.note: Same release. He says he voted for the amendment in both sessions.

findings.passage: In a victory for election security, the State Assembly has approved a proposed amendment to the Wisconsin Constitution that will generally require voters to present a valid photo ID at their polling place.
findings.note: Opening line of his office's release.

findings.passage: During the 2023-2024 legislative session, the Legislature passed constitutional amendments to ensure that only US citizens can vote in Wisconsin elections and to forbid election officials from using private funds, sometimes called “Zuckerbucks”, to administer elections.
findings.note: Same release as published by DrydenWire (page dated Jan 15 2025). Refers to the citizen-only voting amendment.

findings.passage: While I certainly wish that the federal government could be trusted to respect the people’s constitutional rights and that bills like AB 293 weren’t necessary, that trust simply isn’t there right now, at least with regard to the Second Amendment, which is why I supported this proposal.
findings.note: In his own press release, as reprinted by DrydenWire, he explains his cosponsorship and Assembly vote for AB 293, which bars enforcing new federal firearm rules that go beyond Wisconsin's own.
subjects: bar enforcement of new federal gun rules

findings.passage: I’ve heard from a number of constituents who have concerns that the Biden Administration will attempt to curtail Americans’ constitutional right to keep and bear arms,
findings.note: He gives constituent worry about federal limits on the right to keep and bear arms as his reason for AB 293. The release says he cosponsored it.
subjects: bar enforcement of new federal gun rules
